memoryText: And they have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, for they loved not their lives even unto death.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Revelation 12:11 slowly, several times, and try to say it from memory. Then read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This verse holds the secret of the Christian’s victory over Satan. It has three parts.

First, “the blood of the Lamb.” This is the ground of our victory. The accuser has charges against us, but the blood answers every charge. We do not defeat him with our own righteousness but with Christ’s sacrifice, which has already paid the price.

Second, “the word of their testimony.” This is the means. Christians speak the truth about Jesus, about what he has done and who he is, in the face of the lie. Testimony is not only for the pulpit; it includes the plain way we say what we believe at home, at work, and in suffering.

Third, “they loved not their lives even unto death.” This is the cost. Those who are willing to lose their lives for Christ cannot be controlled by fear of death. A person who is not afraid to die cannot be intimidated.

When you feel under spiritual attack, say this verse aloud. Rest in the blood, speak the testimony, and let go of fear.
weekInReview: This week you read through the middle of Revelation. Chapter 7 answered the question “who can stand?” with the sealed servants of God and the great multitude from every nation, robes washed in the blood of the Lamb. Chapter 8 opened the seventh seal with silence in heaven, and the prayers of the saints rising as incense before the throne. Chapters 9 to 11 sounded trumpets of judgment, showed the bitter-sweet little scroll, the two witnesses who are killed and raised, and the seventh trumpet announcing that the kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord. Psalm 141 taught us to pray as incense and to welcome correction. Psalm 150 and Psalm 148 called every creature to praise. Revelation 12 and 13 unveiled the dragon, the woman, and the two beasts, and the church’s way of conquering by the blood of the Lamb, the word of testimony, and willingness to die.
reflectionQuestions: Revelation 12:11 gives three ways the saints conquered the accuser. Which of these three do you rely on most, and which do you tend to neglect?
Most of the world did not repent despite the trumpets (9:20-21). What does this tell you about the limits of judgment and the need for grace? Who are you praying for who needs a change of heart?
The call of 13:10 is for endurance and faith. What is the hardest area in which you need endurance right now? How can the Lamb’s example in Revelation 5 strengthen you?
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for the victory won by his blood.
Ask him for courage to testify.
